summary: The candidate fixes the reported 42-token capture geometry (seven width-six rows rather than eight unequal rows) and fixes the independently reproduced overlapping DSV4 replay-metadata copy on a real ROCm GPU. It does not establish the original Engram contract for genuinely ragged tiers: 43 tokens still captures as [6,6,6,5,5,5,5,5], which is incompatible with the issue's equal-block EngramHasher branch unless that hasher is changed to consume per-request ragged context. This base/candidate has no EngramHasher or Engram model integration, so actual Engram hash outputs and the full first-forward path cannot be verified. The change is therefore a partial fix, not a full original-issue resolution.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual base layout helper returned [6,6,5,5,5,5,5,5], reproducing the 42-token/8-slot geometry behind the Engram assertion.

tests.command: Real-device DSV4RawVerifyMetadata.copy_ overlap reproduction using the prepared interpreter (base)
tests.what_was_measured: On AMD Instinct MI355X, overlapping slices raised RuntimeError: unsupported operation: some elements ... refer to a single memory location.
Candidate regression suite: 14 passed and 5 subtests passed.

tests.command: Independent MI355X adversarial script over token tiers 1,5,6,7,11,12,13,23,24,25,41,42,43,47,48; real RaggedVerifyLayout device prefix sums; overlapping verify/decode metadata views at offsets 0, 1, 2, and -1 (candidate)
tests.what_was_measured: Slot/lens packing invariants, real device qo_indptr and extend_start_loc against an independent Python prefix-sum reference, and alias-safe tensor values. It also demonstrated unequal Engram-incompatible capture rows at non-multiple tiers including 43 tokens.

tests.command: Prepared-interpreter import-path probe at candidate commit
tests.what_was_measured: sglang and changed Python modules imported from /job/repo/python; torch imported from /opt/venv and reported 2.11.0+rocm7.2, HIP 7.2.26015, AMD Instinct MI355X.

gpu_execution.evidence: Real tensors and DSV4 metadata-copy operations ran on the assigned AMD Instinct MI355X. The base overlap failure and candidate success were both observed on device.

remaining_counterexamples: At request width 6, capture_num_slots(43, 6, 8) yields 8 and build_capture_verify_lens yields [6,6,6,5,5,5,5,5]. The original EngramHasher target-verify assertion requires num_tokens == bs * block, so this genuinely ragged tier remains incompatible absent an Engram-side layout-aware change.

Other non-multiple tiers also remain unequal (for example 41 -> [6,6,6,6,6,6,5] and 47 -> [6,6,6,6,6,6,6,5]); no actual per-request Engram hash output could be compared with a reference because the implementation is absent.
The reported full first-forward path after forced-uniform capture was not run with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Only the isolated real-device DSV4 overlap mechanism was reproduced and fixed.
remaining_limitations: The prepared base and exact candidate contain no python/sglang/srt/layers/engram.py, EngramHasher, or DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram integration, so the required per-request hash-context and real hash-output comparison is unsupported in this checkout.
Full TP4/EP4 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash CUDA execution is unavailable on the assigned single AMD ROCm GPU and remains explicitly unverified.
The source report used NVIDIA GB10/CUDA 13.0; this review used AMD Instinct MI355X with ROCm 7.2, so NVIDIA CUDA-graph behavior was not executed.

No C++, FlyDSL, LLVM, or other native source changed in the candidate. A native rebuild was not applicable; imported changed code was confirmed to come from /job/repo/python rather than an installed sglang wheel.
